questions.question:
Which of the following statements are **correct** regarding the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023?
1. The Act applies to courts, including Courts-martial, but excludes affidavits and arbitration.
2. "Document" includes emails, server logs, and smartphone messages.
3. Confessions to police officers are admissible without restriction.
4. The Evidence Act of 1872 is repealed, but pending cases follow the old law.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1, 2, and 4 only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Statement 1:** The **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023**, applies to all judicial proceedings in or before any **Court**, including **Courts-martial** (except those convened under the Army, Navy, and Air Force Acts where specific rules apply). However, it explicitly excludes **affidavits** presented to any Court or Officer and proceedings before an **arbitrator**. **Hence, statement 1 is correct.**
 
• **Statement 2:** Under the new Act, the definition of a **"Document"** has been significantly modernized and expanded to include **electronic and digital records**. This encompasses **emails**, **server logs**, **smartphone messages**, **location data**, and **voicemails**, treating them as documentary evidence. **Hence, statement 2 is correct.**
 
• **Statement 3:** The **BSA, 2023**, maintains the protection against self-incrimination; Section 23 clearly states that any **confession** made to a **police officer** is **not admissible** and cannot be proved against an accused person. This provision is designed to prevent custodial coercion and ensure fair trials. Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.

questions.question: One of the key objectives of India's Venus Orbiter Mission (VOM) is to study the ________ and surface topography of Venus.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**airglow and atmospheric dust**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Venus Orbiter Mission (VOM)**, colloquially known as **Shukrayaan-1**, was officially approved by the **Union Cabinet** of India, chaired by Prime Minister **Narendra Modi**, on **September 18, 2024**.
 
• One of the primary scientific objectives of the mission is to study the **Venusian atmosphere**, specifically focusing on the **airglow** and **atmospheric dust**. This study helps in understanding the chemical processes and the dynamics of the **upper atmosphere** of the planet.
 
• The mission also aims to investigate the **surface topography** and **stratigraphy** of Venus using **high-resolution synthetic aperture radar (SAR)**. This will allow scientists to see through the thick cloud cover that permanently shrouds the planet. ***Hence, the statement regarding airglow and atmospheric dust is correct.***
 
• The **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** is the lead agency responsible for the development and execution of the **Venus Orbiter Mission**. The mission is scheduled for a launch window in **March 2028**, taking advantage of the planetary alignment that occurs roughly every **19 months**.
 
• The total approved budget for the **Venus Orbiter Mission** is approximately **₹1,236 crore**, which includes the cost of the spacecraft, payloads, and the launch vehicle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Venus (The Planet):**
 
 
• **Venus** is often called **Earth’s Twin** due to its similar size and density, but it has a vastly different environment. It is the **hottest planet** in the solar system, with surface temperatures reaching **467°C (872°F)**.
 
• The atmosphere of **Venus** consists of **96.5% Carbon Dioxide** and **3.5% Nitrogen**, leading to a runaway **greenhouse effect**. The atmospheric pressure at the surface is **92 times** that of Earth.
 
 
 
• **VOM Payload and Technology:**
 
 
• The mission will carry several scientific instruments, including **Spectrometers** and **Radars**. These will measure **Solar Wind interactions** with the Venusian **ionosphere** and examine the **shallow subsurface** features.
 
• The mission will use the **LVM3 (Launch Vehicle Mark-3)**, India's most powerful rocket, to propel the orbiter into space.
 
 
 
• **Planetary Orbit:**
 
 
• **Venus** exhibits **retrograde rotation**, meaning it rotates on its axis in the opposite direction to most planets in the solar system, including Earth. A day on **Venus** (one rotation) is longer than its year (one revolution around the **Sun**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Scientific Significance:** By studying **airglow and atmospheric dust**, **ISRO** aims to find clues about why **Venus** evolved so differently from Earth, despite having a similar origin. The study of **dust particles** in the atmosphere provides insights into the **volcanic activity** and **meteoritic impacts** on the planet.
 
• **International Context:** **India** joins a select group of nations, including the **USA (NASA)**, **Europe (ESA)**, and **Russia (Roscosmos)**, that have successfully sent or planned missions to **Venus**.
 
• **Future Outlook:** The data collected by **VOM** will contribute to global scientific knowledge about **exoplanets** and the evolution of **planetary atmospheres**, which is critical for understanding climate change on Earth.

questions.question: Who is in line to become the first woman Chief Justice of the Supreme Court in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Justice B.V. Nagarathna**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Justice B.V. Nagarathna** is slated to become the **first woman Chief Justice of India (CJI)** in **September 2027**. She was born on **October 30, 1962**.
 
• She was elevated to the **Supreme Court of India** on **August 31, 2021**. Her appointment was part of a historic moment where **nine judges** were sworn in simultaneously to the apex court.
 
• She is the daughter of **Justice E.S. Venkataramiah**, who served as the **19th Chief Justice of India** from **June 1989** to **December 1989**. This makes them the first father-daughter duo to both reach the position of Supreme Court judges and potentially the office of the CJI.
 
• Her tenure as **Chief Justice** is expected to be brief, lasting approximately **36 days**, as she will reach the mandatory retirement age of **65 years** in **October 2027**.
 
• Before her elevation to the Supreme Court, she served as a judge of the **Karnataka High Court**, where she was appointed as an additional judge in **2008** and became a permanent judge in **2010**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Justice Anita Sumanth**: She is currently a judge of the **Madras High Court**. She was appointed as an additional judge in **February 2017** and has a strong background in **Direct and Indirect Taxation laws**.
 
• **Justice Sangeeta Chandra**: She serves as a judge at the **Allahabad High Court**. She was elevated to the bench in **September 2016** and has dealt extensively with **civil and constitutional matters**.
 
• **Justice R. Hemalatha**: She was a judge of the **Madras High Court** who retired in **2021**. She began her judicial career in the **Tamil Nadu State Judicial Service** in **1991** before being elevated to the High Court in **2017**.
 
• **Justice M. Fathima Beevi**: Historically, she was the **first female judge** of the Supreme Court of India, appointed in **October 1989**. However, she never held the post of Chief Justice.
 
• **Article 124**: This article of the **Constitution of India** deals with the establishment and constitution of the Supreme Court, including the appointment of judges by the **President of India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Seniority Principle**: The appointment of the **Chief Justice of India** usually follows the **seniority convention**, where the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court is recommended by the outgoing CJI and appointed by the **President**.
 
• **Collegium System**: Judicial appointments to the Supreme Court and High Courts are made via the **Collegium System**, which consists of the **CJI** and the **four senior-most judges** of the Supreme Court.
 
• **Gender Representation**: Since the inception of the Supreme Court on **January 26, 1950**, there has been a significant gender gap. Out of over **250 judges** appointed to the apex court till date, only a small fraction (around **11**) have been women.
 
• **Retirement Rules**: Under the Indian Constitution, Supreme Court judges retire at **65 years**, while High Court judges retire at **62 years**. This age limit is a critical factor in determining the succession line for the **Chief Justice** position.
 
• **Oath of Office**: Every judge of the Supreme Court is required to take an **oath or affirmation** before the **President** or a person appointed by them, as per the **Third Schedule** of the Constitution.
</ul

questions.question: Which Mandal of the Rigveda is devoted to soma drink?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ninth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ninth Mandal** of the **Rigveda** is entirely dedicated to **Soma**, which is both a ritual drink and a Vedic deity. ***Hence, this is the correct answer.***
 
• This particular book contains **114 hymns** (Suktas) addressed to **Soma Pavamana** (the purified Soma). The hymns describe the process of pressing the plant, filtering the juice, and offering it to the gods, especially **Indra**.
 
• The **Rigveda** is the oldest of the four Vedas, consisting of **10 Mandalas** (books) and **1028 hymns**. It was composed roughly between **1500 BCE and 1000 BCE** in the **Sapta-Sindhu** region.
 
• **Soma** was considered the **"King of Plants"** and the drink of immortality (Amrita). The plant was typically found in the **Mujavat mountains**.
 
• The **Ninth Mandal** serves as a collection of hymns that were originally part of other Mandalas but were grouped together because they all relate to the **Soma sacrifice** (Soma Yajna).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Seventh Mandal:** This book is attributed to the sage **Vashistha**. It is famous for mentioning the **Dasharajna War** (Battle of Ten Kings), which took place on the banks of the **Parushni (Ravi) river**. ***Hence, statement A is incorrect.***
 
• **Tenth Mandal:** This is considered the youngest part of the Rigveda. It contains the **Purusha Sukta**, which explains the origin of the **four Varnas** (Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishya, and Shudra) from the body of the **Primeval Being**. It also includes the **Nasadiya Sukta**, which discusses the origin of the universe. ***Hence, this option (though not listed) is significant for social history.***
 
• **Third Mandal:** This Mandal was composed by the sage **Vishvamitra** and contains the **Gayatri Mantra**, which is dedicated to the solar deity **Savitri**.
 
• **Second to Seventh Mandalas:** These are known as the **"Family Books"** (Vansha Mandalas) because they are attributed to specific families of seers like **Gritsamada, Vishvamitra, Vamadeva, Atri, Bharadvaja, and Vashistha**. These are the oldest portions of the Rigveda.
 
• **Structure of Rigveda:** Apart from the Mandalas, the text is divided into **Ashtakas** (eight parts) for easy memorization in the **oral tradition** (Shruti).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Soma Rituals:** The preparation of **Soma** involved crushing the stalks of the plant with stones, filtering the juice through **sheep's wool**, and mixing it with **milk or honey**.
 
• **Deities:** While **Indra** (the god of rain and thunder) is the most prominent deity in the Rigveda with **250 hymns**, **Agni** (the god of fire) follows with **200 hymns**. **Soma** is the third most important deity based on the number of dedicated hymns.
 
• **Historical Context:** The **Rigveda** provides crucial information about the **Early Vedic Period**, including the transition from nomadic life to settled agriculture and the early political structures of **tribal chiefdoms** (Rajan).
 
• **UNESCO Recognition:** The **Rigveda** was included in **UNESCO's Memory of the World Register** in **2007** due to its significance as a foundational text of human civilization and the **Sanskrit language**.
</ul

• The most fundamental objective of deficit financing in developing nations like **India** is **to stimulate economic growth**. • It serves as a crucial method for **resource mobilization** to fund **Five-Year Plans** and other large-scale developmental projects that private sectors might find unprofitable or too capital-intensive.
 
• Deficit financing is often used to **curb unemployment**. During periods of economic slowdown, increased government spending increases **aggregate demand**, leading to higher production and job creation. *Hence, the statement about decreasing money supply is incorrect as deficit financing actually increases it.*

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a reason for a fiscal deficit?

options.text: High government expenditure on welfare schemes
Surplus in the balance of payments

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Surplus in the balance of payments**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fiscal Deficit** is defined as the excess of the **government's total expenditure** over its **total revenue**, excluding **borrowings**, during a specific **financial year**. It indicates the total **borrowing requirements** of the government.
 
• **High government expenditure on welfare schemes:** When the **government** increases spending on **social welfare**, **subsidies**, and **infrastructure** without a corresponding increase in **revenue**, the gap between income and expenditure widens. ***Hence, this statement is a correct reason for a fiscal deficit.***
 
• **Reduction in tax revenue:** A decline in **tax collection**, whether due to **economic slowdown**, **tax evasion**, or **tax cuts** implemented by the **Ministry of Finance**, reduces the **government's income**. This shortfall directly contributes to the **budgetary gap**. ***Hence, this statement is a correct reason for a fiscal deficit.***
 
• **Increase in public borrowings:** While **borrowing** is a way to finance a **deficit**, high levels of **public debt** lead to massive **interest payments** in subsequent years. These interest payments are a form of **revenue expenditure** that further inflates the **fiscal deficit**. ***Hence, this statement is a correct reason for a fiscal deficit.***
 
• **Surplus in the balance of payments:** This occurs when a **country's** total **exports** and **capital inflows** exceed its **imports** and **capital outflows**. This is an **international trade** metric and does not represent a shortfall in the **domestic budget** of the **government**. ***Hence, this statement is NOT a reason for a fiscal deficit.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Revenue Deficit:** This refers to the excess of **revenue expenditure** over **revenue receipts**. It signifies that the **government** is unable to cover its **day-to-day operational expenses** (like salaries and pensions) from its regular income.
 
• **Primary Deficit:** This is the **Fiscal Deficit** minus the **interest payments** on previous **borrowings**. It shows how much the **government** needs to borrow to meet its **current year** expenses, excluding the burden of **past debt**.
 
• **Fiscal Policy:** In **India**, fiscal policy is the tool used by the **Union Government** to monitor and influence the **economy** by adjusting **spending levels** and **tax rates**. It is managed primarily through the **Union Budget** presented every **February**.
 
• **Sources of Revenue:** The **government** earns through **tax revenue** (Direct taxes like **Income Tax** and **Corporate Tax**, and Indirect taxes like **GST**) and **non-tax revenue** (interest receipts, **dividends** from **PSUs**, and **external grants**).
 
• **Capital Receipts:** These include **recoveries of loans**, **disinvestment** of **Public Sector Undertakings**, and **borrowings**. Unlike **revenue receipts**, these either create a **liability** or reduce the **assets** of the **government**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **FRBM Act, 2003:** The **Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act** was enacted to ensure **inter-generational equity** in **fiscal management** and long-term **macro-economic stability**. It aimed to limit the **fiscal deficit** to **3% of the GDP**.
 
• **Deficit Financing:** To bridge the **fiscal gap**, the **government** may borrow from the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** or the **public**. If the **RBI** prints new **currency** to fund the **deficit**, it can lead to high **inflation** in the **economy**.
 
• **Impact of High Deficit:** Persistent **fiscal deficits** can lead to a **debt trap**, **crowding out** of **private investment** (as the **government** consumes most of the **market credit**), and a decrease in the **sovereign credit rating** of the **country**.
 
• **Grants-in-aid:** Under **Article 275** of the **Constitution of India**, the **Union** provides **grants** to **states**, which is a major **expenditure** item that impacts the **fiscal deficit** of the **Central Government**.
</ul

questions.question: What is the role of the ribosome in a cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Protein synthesis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary role of the **ribosome** in a cell is **protein synthesis**. Ribosomes act as the cellular machinery that translates genetic code into functional proteins, which are essential for all life processes. ***Hence, the correct option is Protein synthesis.***
 
• Ribosomes are composed of two major components: **ribosomal RNA (rRNA)** and **proteins**. They consist of a **large subunit** and a **small subunit** that come together during the process of translation.
 
• In a cell, ribosomes can be found in two locations: either floating freely in the **cytoplasm** or attached to the surface of the **Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER)**. Proteins synthesized on the **RER** are typically destined for secretion or membrane insertion, while free ribosomes synthesize proteins for use within the **cytoplasm**.
 
• The process conducted by ribosomes is known as **Translation**. During this phase, the ribosome reads the sequence of the **messenger RNA (mRNA)** and, with the help of **transfer RNA (tRNA)**, assembles **amino acids** in the correct order to form a **polypeptide chain**.
 
• Ribosomes are universal organelles, meaning they are found in both **prokaryotic** (e.g., bacteria) and **eukaryotic** (e.g., plants and animals) cells, highlighting their fundamental importance in biology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Discovery and Characteristics:**
 
 
• Ribosomes were first observed in the mid-**1950s** by the Romanian-American cell biologist **George Palade** using an electron microscope. He was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine** in **1974** for this discovery.
 
• In **prokaryotes**, the ribosomes are smaller, known as **70S** ribosomes (consisting of **30S** and **50S** subunits). In **eukaryotes**, they are larger, known as **80S** ribosomes (consisting of **40S** and **60S** subunits). The **"S"** stands for the **Svedberg unit**, a measure of sedimentation rate.
 
 
 
• **Energy Production (Option A):**
 
 
• **Energy production** is the primary function of the **Mitochondria**, often called the "Powerhouse of the cell." This organelle generates **Adenosine Triphosphate (ATP)** through the process of **cellular respiration**. ***Hence, statement A is incorrect regarding ribosomes.***
 
 
 
• **Cell Division (Option C):**
 
 
• The process of **cell division** is facilitated by organelles like **centrioles** and **centrosomes** in animal cells, which help in the formation of **spindle fibers**. The **nucleus** plays the leading role by managing **DNA replication**. ***Hence, statement C is incorrect regarding ribosomes.***
 
 
 
• **Transport of Substances (Option D):**
 
 
• The **transport of substances** within and out of the cell is handled by the **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)** and the **Golgi Apparatus** (or Golgi Complex). The Golgi apparatus acts as a "post office," packaging and labeling proteins for their specific **locations**. ***Hence, statement D is incorrect regarding ribosomes.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ribozymes:** While most enzymes are proteins, some **RNA** molecules in the ribosome possess catalytic activity. These are called **ribozymes**, and they are responsible for forming the **peptide bonds** between amino acids.
 
• **Antibiotic Target:** Because **bacterial (70S)** ribosomes differ in structure from **human (80S)** ribosomes, many **antibiotics** (such as **Tetracycline** and **Erythromycin**) work by specifically targeting and inhibiting bacterial ribosomes without harming the host's cells.
 
• **Polysomes:** Often, multiple ribosomes attach to a single **mRNA** strand simultaneously to produce multiple copies of a protein quickly; this complex is known as a **polyribosome** or **polysome**.
</ul

questions.question: Which book by Anirudh Kanisetti, exploring the history of Southern India, was awarded the Yuva Puraskar?

• The work covers a period of approximately **five centuries**, starting from the **6th Century CE**, and highlights how these empires shaped the cultural and political landscape of the **Indian subcontinent**.
 
• It aims to challenge the **North-centric** view of **Indian history** by bringing the complex geopolitics and achievements of **Southern India** to the forefront of mainstream historical discourse.

• **Lords of the Deccan:** This work by **Anirudh Kanisetti** is the correct book that explores **Southern Indian** history and won the **Yuva Puraskar** in **2023**. *Hence, statement C is correct.*

• The **Sahitya Akademi**, India's **National Academy of Letters**, was established on **12 March 1954** and functions as an autonomous organization under the **Ministry of Culture**.

__
 
• The **India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC)** was officially announced on the sidelines of the **G20 Summit** held in **New Delhi** in **September 2023**, specifically identifying **Saudi Arabia** and the **UAE** as critical partners.
 
• **Saudi Arabia** and **India** have deepened their clean energy dialogue through a memorandum of understanding (**MoU**) signed in **2023**, which focuses on **electrical interconnection**, **green hydrogen**, and establishing secure supply chains between the two **Middle Eastern** and **South Asian** nations.
 
• The **UAE** is a pivotal trade partner, having signed the **Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA)** with **India**, which became effective on **May 1, 2022**. This agreement serves as a blueprint for the trade and investment dialogues integrated into the **IMEC** framework.
 
• The dialogue aims to facilitate a **cross-border ship-to-rail transit network**, where **UAE** and **Saudi Arabian** ports and rail lines will bridge the gap between **India** and the **European** markets.
 
• These dialogues are not limited to physical goods but extend to **digital connectivity** and **clean energy cables**, ensuring that the **UAE** and **Saudi Arabia** act as energy hubs for **India’s** future sustainable growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **IMEC Structure**: The corridor is divided into two distinct parts: the **East Corridor**, which connects **India** to the **Arabian Gulf**, and the **Northern Corridor**, which links the **Arabian Gulf** to **Europe**.
 
• **Global Participants**: Besides **India**, **Saudi Arabia**, and the **UAE**, the other signatories include the **United States of America (USA)**, the **European Union**, **France**, **Germany**, and **Italy**.
 
• **Trade Efficiency**: Once fully operational, the **IMEC** is projected to reduce shipping costs by approximately **40%** and decrease transit time by **15%** compared to the current **Suez Canal** route.
 
• **Green Hydrogen Focus**: **Saudi Arabia** and the **UAE** are investing heavily in **renewable energy** under their respective national visions (like **Saudi Vision 2030**), making them ideal partners for **India’s National Green Hydrogen Mission**.
 
• **Economic Integration**: The **IMEC** is viewed as a strategic alternative to **China’s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI)**, focusing on **transparency**, **sovereignty**, and **sustainable debt** practices.

• **Geopolitical Impact**: This partnership strengthens **India’s** **"Link West" policy**, positioning the country as a central node in the global supply chain between **East Asia** and the **Western world**.
 
• **Strategic MoUs**: In **February 2024**, during the visit of the **Indian Prime Minister** to the **UAE**, further **intergovernmental framework agreements** were signed to fast-track the **IMEC** implementation despite regional challenges.
 
• **Role of Ports**: Key ports involved in the dialogue include **Mundra** and **Kandla** in **India**, **Jebel Ali** in the **UAE**, and **Dammam** and **Ras Al-Khair** in **Saudi Arabia**.
</ul

questions.question: What is the function of the "Speak Up!" portal launched by NADA (National Anti Doping Agency)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Report Anti-Doping Rule Violations confidentially**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA)** India launched the **"Speak Up!"** portal as a secure and confidential digital platform dedicated to reporting **Anti-Doping Rule Violations (ADRV)**. This function allows individuals to report suspicious activities without fear of repercussions. ***Hence, the statement regarding reporting violations is correct.***
 
• The primary **use** of this portal is to protect the **integrity** of sports in **India** by encouraging **whistleblowers**, including **athletes**, **coaches**, and **support personnel**, to share sensitive information about doping.
 
• The **"Speak Up!"** portal ensures **anonymity**, meaning the identity of the informant is strictly protected under the guidelines of the **World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA)**. This **feature** is critical for gathering intelligence that may not be available through routine testing.
 
• The portal is a key component of **NADA's** **Intelligence and Investigations** framework. It focuses on catching not just the athletes who use **banned substances**, but also the wider network of **suppliers** and **facilitators** involved in doping rings.
 
• By providing a dedicated **online platform**, **NADA** aims to foster a **clean sports culture** where stakeholders feel empowered to contribute to a **dope-free environment**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA):** It was established as a registered society under the **Societies Registration Act** on **November 24, 2005**. It functions under the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**, Government of **India**.
 
• **WADA (World Anti-Doping Agency):** Founded on **November 10, 1999**, in **Lausanne, Switzerland**, and now headquartered in **Montreal, Canada**. **WADA** sets the **Global Anti-Doping Code**, which **NADA** India follows to maintain international standards in **drug testing** and **adjudication**.
 
• **Therapeutic Use Exemptions (TUE):** This is a process where an **athlete** can request permission to use a **prohibited substance** for legitimate **medical reasons**. Applications are reviewed by a **TUE Committee** consisting of **medical experts** to ensure no unfair advantage is gained.
 
• **Banned Substances:** These are listed annually by **WADA** in the **Prohibited List**. Categories include **Anabolic Agents**, **Peptide Hormones**, **Stimulants**, and **Glucocorticoids**. The list is updated every **year**, effective from **January 1st**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Anti-Doping Rule Violations (ADRV):** Under the **2021 WADA Code**, there are **11** distinct violations. These include the **presence** of a substance, **attempted use**, **refusing** a sample collection, **whereabouts failures**, and **trafficking**.
 
• **Dope Testing Process:** **NADA** conducts both **In-Competition** and **Out-of-Competition** testing. Samples (blood or urine) are analyzed at **WADA-accredited laboratories**. In **India**, the **National Dope Testing Laboratory (NDTL)** is the primary facility for analysis.
 
• **Consequences of Doping:** Athletes found guilty of an **ADRV** face sanctions including **disqualification** of results, **forfeiture** of medals, and **period of ineligibility** (bans) ranging from a **few months** to a **lifetime ban** for repeat offenders.
 
• **The Registered Testing Pool (RTP):** High-level athletes must provide their **location** and **contact details** for **one hour** every **day** to allow for **unannounced testing**. Failure to provide this **data** three times in **12 months** constitutes an **ADRV**.
</ul

questions.question: When was BIMSTEC established?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1997**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **BIMSTEC**, which stands for the **Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation**, was officially established on **6 June 1997**.
 
• The organization came into existence through the signing of the **Bangkok Declaration**, which served as the founding document for this regional group.
 
• Initially, the group was formed with four member states and was known as **BIST-EC** (**Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, and Thailand** Economic Cooperation).
 
• Following the inclusion of **Myanmar** on **22 December 1997** during a special Ministerial Meeting in **Bangkok**, the group was renamed **BIMST-EC**.
 
• In **February 2004**, the organization expanded further as **Nepal** and **Bhutan** became full members, leading to the current name adopted during the first summit in **Bangkok**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geographic Scope:** **BIMSTEC** is a unique regional organization that brings together seven countries from **South Asia** and **Southeast Asia**, creating a bridge between the two regions. Five members are from **South Asia** (**Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal, and Sri Lanka**) and two are from **Southeast Asia** (**Myanmar and Thailand**).
 
• **Secretariat:** The permanent secretariat of **BIMSTEC** is located in **Dhaka, Bangladesh**. It was formally inaugurated in **2014** to coordinate the activities and implementation of various projects.
 
• **Areas of Cooperation:** Originally, the cooperation started with **six sectors** including **trade, technology, energy, transport, tourism, and fisheries**. It has since expanded to **14 sectors**, including **agriculture, public health, poverty alleviation, counter-terrorism, and climate change**.
 
• **Strategic Significance for India:** For **India**, **BIMSTEC** has become a primary platform for regional cooperation under its **Neighborhood First** and **Act East Policy**, especially as activities in **SAARC** (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) have remained stalled.
 
• **Economic Potential:** The **Bay of Bengal** region is home to approximately **1.5 billion people**, accounting for about **22% of the global population**, and has a combined **GDP** of over **USD 3.8 trillion** as of recent estimates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Institutional Reforms:** During the **5th BIMSTEC Summit** hosted virtually by **Sri Lanka** in **March 2022**, the **BIMSTEC Charter** was signed and adopted. This provided the organization with a formal legal identity and a specific flag and emblem.
 
• **Lead Countries:** Each member state leads specific pillars of cooperation. For instance, **India** leads the **Security** pillar, which includes **counter-terrorism, transnational crime, and disaster management**.
 
• **Connectivity:** A major focus of the group is the **BIMSTEC Master Plan for Transport Connectivity**, which aims to enhance physical connectivity through roads, railways, and maritime routes to boost regional trade.
 
• **Milestones:** The year **2022** marked the **25th anniversary** of the founding of **BIMSTEC**, highlighting a quarter-century of effort toward regional integration in the **Bay of Bengal** rim.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**China**__.

__
 
• The **South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC)** is a regional intergovernmental organization and geopolitical union of states in **South Asia**. It was established with the signing of the **SAARC Charter** in **Dhaka** on **8 December 1985**.
 
• The organization currently has **8 member countries**: **Afghanistan**, **Bangladesh**, **Bhutan**, **India**, **Maldives**, **Nepal**, **Pakistan**, and **Sri Lanka**.
 
• **Afghanistan** became the **8th member** of **SAARC** during the **14th SAARC Summit** held in **New Delhi** in **April 2007**. Prior to this, there were only seven founding members. Hence, statement 1 is correct.
 
• **Bhutan** is one of the founding members of the association and has been an active participant since its inception in **1985**. Hence, statement 2 is correct.
 
• **China** holds the status of an **Observer Country** in **SAARC**, but it is not a formal member of the association. The association currently has **9 observers**, including **Australia**, **China**, the **European Union**, **Iran**, **Japan**, **Mauritius**, **Myanmar**, **South Korea**, and the **United States**. Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.
 
• **Nepal** is a founding member and currently hosts the **SAARC Secretariat**, which was established in **Kathmandu** on **16 January 1987**. Hence, statement 4 is correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Objectives of SAARC:**
 
 
• The primary objective of **SAARC** is to promote the **welfare of the peoples of South Asia** and to improve their quality of life through **accelerated economic growth**, **social progress**, and **cultural development** in the region.
 
• It aims to provide all individuals the opportunity to live in dignity and to realize their full potentials by strengthening **collective self-reliance** among the countries of **South Asia**.
 
 
 
• **Secretariat and Administration:**
 
 
• The **SAARC Secretariat** is headed by a **Secretary-General**, who is appointed by the **Council of Ministers** from Member States in alphabetical order for a **three-year term**.
 
• The first **Secretary-General** was **Abul Ahsan** from **Bangladesh**. The current **Secretariat** is located in **Kathmandu**, **Nepal**.
 
 
 
• **Specialized Bodies of SAARC:**
 
 
• **South Asian University (SAU)**: An international university established by the eight member nations of **SAARC**, located in **India** (**New Delhi**).
 
• **SAARC Development Fund (SDF)**: Its primary objective is to promote the welfare of the people of the **SAARC region**, with its secretariat located in **Thimphu**, **Bhutan**.
 
• **SAARC Arbitration Council (SARCO)**: An inter-governmental body located in **Islamabad**, **Pakistan**, to provide a legal framework for the settlement of commercial and trade disputes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Principles of SAARC:**
 
 
• Cooperation within the framework of the association is based on respect for the principles of **sovereign equality**, **territorial integrity**, **political independence**, and **non-interference** in the internal affairs of other states.
 
• Decisions at all levels in **SAARC** are taken on the basis of **unanimity**, and **bilateral and contentious issues** are excluded from the deliberations of the association.
 
 
 
• **SAARC Charter Day:**
 
 
• Every **year**, **8 December** is observed as **SAARC Charter Day** to mark the adoption of the **SAARC Charter** in **1985**.
 
 
 
• **South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA):**
 
 
• **SAFTA** was reached at the **12th SAARC Summit** at **Islamabad**, **Pakistan** on **6 January 2004**. It aims to reduce **customs duties** of all traded goods to **zero percent** by the **year 2016**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: What type of services does NIRTAR provide?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Swami Vivekanand National Institute of Rehabilitation Training and Research (SVNIRTAR)** is a premier autonomous body under the **Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (Divyangjan)**, which falls under the **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment**, Government of India.
 
• The institute is located at **Olatpur**, approximately **30 km** from **Cuttack** and **Bhubaneswar** in **Odisha**. It was originally established as an **Artificial Limbs Centre** in **1975** and later upgraded to a **National Institute** in **1984**.
 
• The core mission of the institute is to provide comprehensive **rehabilitation services**, high-quality **education**, and conduct pioneering **research** in the field of **locomotor disabilities**. Hence, the statement regarding rehabilitation, education, and research is correct.
 
• It functions as a **referral center** for the rehabilitation of persons with locomotor disabilities, providing specialized treatments such as **Physiotherapy**, **Occupational Therapy**, and **Prosthetics and Orthotics**.
 
• The institute maintains a **100-bed hospital** where **reconstructive surgeries** are performed to correct deformities caused by **Polio**, **Cerebral Palsy**, and **congenital anomalies**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Educational Programs:** SVNIRTAR offers several professional undergraduate and postgraduate courses. Key programs include **Bachelor of Physiotherapy (BPT)**, **Bachelor of Occupational Therapy (BOT)**, and **Bachelor of Prosthetics and Orthotics (BPO)**. It also offers **Post Graduate (DNB/MS)** courses in **Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation (PMR)**.
 
• **Other National Institutes:** The **Government of India** has established several other institutes for different types of disabilities:
 
 
• **NIEPVD (National Institute for the Empowerment of Persons with Visual Disabilities)** located in **Dehradun**.
 
• **AYJNISHD (Ali Yavar Jung National Institute of Speech and Hearing Disabilities)** located in **Mumbai**.
 
• **NIEPMD (National Institute for Empowerment of Persons with Multiple Disabilities)** located in **Chennai**.
 
• **PDUNIPPD (Pt. Deendayal Upadhyaya National Institute for Persons with Physical Disabilities)** located in **New Delhi**.
 
 
 
• **Research and Development:** The institute focuses on designing and developing **low-cost aids and appliances** for the disabled. Research is conducted to improve **surgical techniques** and **therapeutic interventions** for better patient outcomes.
 
• **Extension Services:** SVNIRTAR also manages various **Composite Regional Centres (CRCs)** and **District Disability Rehabilitation Centres (DDRCs)** to provide services in rural and remote areas of **India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legal Framework:** The functioning of such institutes is aligned with the **Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016**, which ensures the **full and effective participation** and inclusion of persons with disabilities in society.
 
• **Beneficiaries:** The institute serves thousands of patients annually, particularly those from **economically weaker sections**. Many services, including the distribution of **assistive devices** under the **ADIP Scheme (Assistance to Disabled Persons for Purchase/Fitting of Aids and Appliances)**, are provided free of cost or at highly subsidized rates.
 
• **Impact:** Through its **human resource development** programs, SVNIRTAR has produced thousands of **rehabilitation professionals** who serve in various hospitals and NGOs across the **globe**.
</ul

questions.question: Which is the largest container port in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jawaharlal Nehru Port (JNPT), Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru Port**, also widely known as **Nhava Sheva**, is the largest **container port** in India. It is located in **Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra**, along the **Arabian Sea** coast.
 
• It was commissioned on **May 26, 1989**, with the primary objective of de-congesting the **Mumbai Port** and serving as a hub for containerized traffic in the country.
 
• The port handles approximately **50%** of the total containerized cargo across all **major ports** in India. It is currently ranked among the top **30** container ports globally in terms of efficiency and volume.
 
• It serves as the gateway for India's international trade, particularly with **Europe, the Middle East, and the Americas**. The port handles diverse commodities including **textiles, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, carpets, and heavy machinery**.
 
• JNPT is the first major port in India to adopt the **Landlord Port Model**, where the port authority acts as a regulatory body and landlord, while port operations are carried out by **private terminal operators**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mundra Port, Gujarat**:
 
 
• Located in the **Kutch district** of **Gujarat**, it is the largest **private port** and the largest **commercial port** in India by overall cargo volume.
 
• It is operated by **Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Limited (APSEZ)** and has surpassed many major government ports in total tonnage handled annually.
 
 
 
• **Chennai Port, Tamil Nadu**:
 
 
• It is the **second largest** container port in India and the largest port in the **Bay of Bengal** region.
 
• Established in **1881**, it is an **artificial and all-weather port** that plays a crucial role in the handling of **automobiles, iron ore, and agricultural products**.
 
 
 
• **Kolkata Port, West Bengal**:
 
 
• Officially renamed the **Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port** in **2020**, it is the only **major riverine port** in India.
 
• Located about **203 kilometers** from the sea on the banks of the **Hooghly River**, it serves as a critical trade link for **North-East India** and landlocked neighbors like **Nepal and Bhutan**.
 
 
 
• **Mumbai Port, Maharashtra**:
 
 
• It is one of the **oldest modern ports** in India, used primarily for **bulk cargo** and **liquid chemicals**. Unlike JNPT, it is a **natural deep-water harbor**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Infrastructure and Connectivity**: **JNPT** is directly connected to the **Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (WDFC)**, which significantly reduces the transit time for goods moving between the port and the **National Capital Region (NCR)**.
 
• **TEU Capacity**: The port's performance is measured in **TEUs (Twenty-foot Equivalent Units)**. In the financial year **2022-2023**, JNPT handled a record-breaking **6.05 million TEUs**.
 
• **Special Economic Zone (SEZ)**: A dedicated **Multi-Product SEZ** has been developed at JNPT to promote **manufacturing-led exports** and enhance the "Make in India" initiative.
 
• **Digital Initiatives**: The port has implemented the **Centralized Parking Plaza (CPP)** and **Direct Port Delivery (DPD)** systems to ensure **transparency** and reduce the **Logistics Performance Index (LPI)** costs for traders.
</ul

questions.question: The term "Jana" in the Rig Vedic period primarily referred to a:

options.text: Tribe or a group of related families.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tribe or a group of related families**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **Rig Vedic period** (roughly **1500 BCE to 1000 BCE**), the term **Jana** primarily denoted a **tribe** or a collective of people bound by **kinship ties**.
 
• The **Rig Veda**, the oldest of the four Vedas, mentions the word **Jana** approximately **275 times**, signifying its central role as the highest social and political unit of that era.
 
• The leader or protector of the **Jana** was known as the **Rajan** (often referred to as **Gopati Janasya** or protector of the people), whose main responsibility was the protection of the tribe and its cattle.
 
• The **Jana** was essentially a **pastoral and nomadic** unit; during this period, the concept of a fixed **territorial state** (Janapada) had not yet emerged, as the people frequently moved in search of pastures.
 
• Membership in the **Jana** was determined by **birth and blood relations**, making it a cohesive socio-political entity rather than a geographical one.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Social Hierarchy:**
 
 
• The **Kula** (family) was the smallest unit, headed by the **Kulapa**.
 
• A group of families formed a **Grama** (village), headed by a **Gramani**.
 
• Several **Gramas** formed a **Vis** (clan), headed by a **Vispati**.
 
• Multiple **Vis** units combined to form the **Jana** (tribe).
 
 
 
• **Political Assemblies:**
 
 
• The **Jana** participated in tribal assemblies such as the **Sabha**, **Samiti**, **Vidatha**, and **Gana**.
 
• The **Samiti** was a folk assembly of the entire **Jana** where major decisions, including the election of the **Rajan**, were discussed.
 
 
 
• **Tribal Conflicts:**
 
 
• Wars between different **Janas** were common and were usually fought for cattle (**Gavisthi**).
 
• A famous example is the **Battle of the Ten Kings** (**Dasrajanaya**), where the **Bharata Jana** emerged victorious against a confederacy of ten other tribes on the banks of the river **Parushni** (modern-day **Ravi**).
 
 
 
• **Evolution to Janapada:**
 
 
• By the **Later Vedic period** (**1000 BCE to 600 BCE**), as tribes settled into agriculture, **Janas** merged to form larger **territorial units** known as **Janapadas**.
 
• Examples include the **Kurus** and **Panchalas**, which were formed by the merging of smaller **Rig Vedic** tribes like the **Bharatas** and **Purus**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Economic Features:** The **Jana** economy was largely **pastoral**. Cows were the most valued possession and served as a unit of **currency** and wealth.
 
• **Geographical Location:** The **Rig Vedic Janas** were initially concentrated in the **Sapta-Sindhu** region, which includes the **Indus River** and its tributaries in modern-day **India** and **Pakistan**.
 
• **Administrative Functions:** The **Rajan** did not have a standing army or a formal **taxation system**. He received voluntary contributions called **Bali** from the members of the **Jana**.
 
• **Women's Participation:** In the early **Rig Vedic** society, women had the right to attend tribal assemblies like the **Sabha** and **Vidatha**, reflecting a relatively egalitarian social structure within the **Jana**.
</ul
